newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea's January car sales plunge on strikes.
newsitem.headline: South Korea's January car sales plunge on strikes.

text.p: South Korean car sales plummeted in January as strikes against the country's major industries crippled production, automakers said on Tuesday.
Hyundai Motor Co Ltd, the nation's largest car producer, said its vehicle sales plunged to 48,432 units in January from 106,885 the previous year.
"The drop was due largely to strikes that lasted for about a month (until) January 20," said Hyundai spokesman Min Kyung-hwan.
He said exports in January totalled 16,768 units, down from 43,818 a year ago.
"Strikes between December 26 and January 20 cost the company about 80,000 units in lost production," Min said.
Workers at the nation's major industries walked out in protest at the forced parliamentary passage of a labour law that allows employers to lay off workers.
In 1996, Hyundai Motor sold 1.31 million units, up from 1.23 million units in the previous year.
Hyundai, flagship of the Hyundai Group HYGR.CN, has set this year's sales target at 1.45 million units, of which 650,000 units are for export.
Min said weakening local demand as a result of an economic downturn contributed to the January sales decline.
Kia Motors Corp, one of South Korea's leading carmakers, said its sales dropped to 26,459 units in January from 63,165 a year ago.
A Kia spokesman said strikes, which lasted until mid-January in the company, cost it 35,400 units in lost production.
He said exports in the month totalled 11,654 units, down from 20,135 a year before.
Kia said it aimed to sell 950,000 vehicles in 1997, 410,000 of them exports. In 1996, Kia sold a total of 781,250 units, including exports of 322,850.
Last week Kia said union workers agreed to work at weekends to make up for losses from strikes.
Normally, Kia workers take holidays on Sundays and on every other Saturday.
Daewoo Motor Co, a unit of the Daewoo Group, said its vehicle sales fell to 45,914 units in January from 48,935 a year ago.
The company's vehicle exports during the month dropped to 23,019 units from 24,206 units a year ago.
A Daewoo statement said its passenger car sales totalled 32,721 units in January, down from 41,162 units in January 1996.
